newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields edge up, crown soft on budget.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields edge up, crown soft on budget.

text.p: Swedish debt yields rose slightly in morning trade on Tuesday while the crown weakened against the mark amid leaks of Sweden's supplementary budget.
"The market is viewing the budget a bit more negatively now. Some assumptions made by the government seem a bit too optimistic," one dealer said.
He said risk is on the upside but a strong Europe was preventing debt yields from rising further.
"But we may well spread apart," he said.
Six month T-bill rate rose one basis point to 4.09 percent after opening one basis point lower at 4.07 percent.
Ten year bond yields were flat at 7.16 percent by midday after dipping one basis point at the open.
The crown weakened after some days of firming.
"The crown softened on profit-taking and there is no more positive information to go on," one dealer said.
He also said the budget was more likely to present the market with negative measures than positive.
The crown softened to 4.4425 crowns compared to 4.4235 crowns on Monday.
